abstract_sentences.text: We study the revenue of approximate correlated equilibrium in discrete first price auctions - the set of allowable bids is B = {0, 1/k, . . . , 1 − 1/k, 1} for some k ∈ N.
We show that the revenue of any ϵ-approximate correlated equilibrium is at least v2 − Θ(1/k) − Θ(ϵk2), where v2 ≥ 0 is the second-highest valuation.
Our results establish the first polynomial convergence rates on the revenue generated by no-swap regret bidders in first-price auctions.
For instance, if bidders admit the optimal swap regret of O(√kT), then the time-averaged revenue is at least v2 − Θ(1/k) − Θ(ϵ) after O(k5/ϵ2) rounds.

final_judgment.single_storyline: Finite-time no-swap learning is reduced to approximate-CE revenue minimization; an LP dual fitting produces v2-3/k-Theta(epsilon k^2), then yields a finite-horizon corollary [p. 5, Section 3, 'linear program'].
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: The body keeps the problem, auction/CE model, regret bridge, main LP and dual assignment, one representative case proof, three main figures, and the open rate gap [pp. 1-10].
final_judgment.appendix_moves: Appendix A gives the alternate [19] argument, B/C/D supply deferred proofs, and E holds Bayesian simulation detail [pp. 15-25].
final_judgment.best_pattern: The strongest structure is exact-CE baseline to quasi-polynomial obstruction to LP/dual proof to finite-time corollary [pp. 2, 5-7].
final_judgment.largest_gap: The epsilon k^2 versus epsilon gap remains open; Bayesian plots lack replication, uncertainty, and a quantitative CDF distance [p. 10; pp. 23-25].
final_judgment.transfer_rule: For a rate improvement, retain the core reduction, decisive assignment, and one representative proof in the body, then immediately translate the theorem into the operational finite-horizon consequence [pp. 5-9].
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: This rule suits compact theory work. When empirical evidence bears a central conclusion, a single time-average trajectory or visual CDF overlay does not establish across-run stability [pp. 9-10, 23-25].
